name: ClubAL
summary: ClubAL brings routines, consultation and operational information together in one place. The current modules remain available while a new web version of Operador is developed and validated.
role: Product direction and development of the local-first foundation, including responsibility boundaries and the evolution of Operador to the web.
evidence: Screens with demonstration data document Operação, Rotinas, Consulta and the integrated weather forecast in the current Windows modules.
promise: Operational information stays organized and available to each environment without giving everyone editing access.
showcaseSubtitle: Organizes the recording, publishing and consultation of routines across institutional environments.

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Operational information gets lost when every environment improvises.
tabs.body: Spreadsheets, paper and scattered messages create different versions of the same routine. ClubAL centralizes records on the responsible PC and separates editing from reading.

tabs.label: Contribution
tabs.title: The operation was divided by responsibility, not by technical convenience.
tabs.body: I structured the product to separate those who record and publish from those who only consult. This decision reduces unintended editing and keeps one local source of approved information.

tabs.label: How it works
tabs.title: Each part supports a moment in the routine.
tabs.body: Operação records and publishes; Rotinas displays approved content in each environment; Consulta provides authorized reading without opening editing.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: A new web version of Operador is in development.
tabs.body: Operação, Rotinas and Consulta remain available in the Windows modules. The new web version of Operador is under validation with synthetic data.

name: Maeve Roscaern
kicker: A dark fantasy RPG built for solo production
summary: Maeve Roscaern is an original single-player RPG developed at a compact scale for a solo production.
role: Creative direction, systems design and prototype implementation in a solo production.
evidence: Light combo, dodge and Blood First now form the first Phase 8 combat slice.
promise: Dun Caerwyn turns blood, memory and choices into persistent marks.
showcaseSubtitle: Turns an original universe into a playable experience by combining narrative, systems and a viable scope for independent production.

tabs.label: Game
tabs.title: An adult protagonist in a world that records consequences.
tabs.body: Dun Caerwyn, House Roscaern and its systems make body, blood and memory shape Maeve’s journey, narrative and combat.

tabs.label: Production
tabs.title: The scale is designed for one person to finish.
tabs.body: Compact areas, modular kits and concentrated detail preserve the mood without promising a world larger than solo production can support.

tabs.label: The Architect
tabs.title: The Architect connects authorship and consequence.
tabs.body: My image as The Architect is a conceptual easter egg about authorship and consequence. It inspires the project without claiming that the character is already playable.
points: Concept is not presented as gameplay

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The first combat slice is implemented.
tabs.body: Light combo, dodge and Blood First now form part of Phase 8. The next stage focuses on playtesting and adjustments to combat feel, pace and legibility.

name: Demonyza
kicker: Digital presence case for a content creator
summary: The website brings profile, schedule, streams and community together in a responsive experience for mobile and desktop.
role: Product direction, content architecture, responsive design and publication of the client’s website.
evidence: A live website available on mobile and desktop, with a profile, schedule and public paths to the community.
promise: Content and community in an original digital presence that is recognizable and easy to navigate.
imageAlt: Current Demonyza homepage with purple visual identity, navigation and interactive areas

tabs.label: Challenge
tabs.title: More than a link page.
tabs.body: The starting point was to introduce the creator, organize her public channels and give the community clear routes without erasing the client’s identity.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: The client’s identity, with clear navigation.
tabs.body: Profile, schedule, Twitch, Discord and OpenDota form an original responsive experience for mobile and desktop.
points: Easy return to the main flow

tabs.label: Delivery
tabs.title: Live and maintained independently.
tabs.body: The website is live on Cloudflare Pages; the client’s code remains protected in a private repository.

name: Codex Checkpoint
kicker: A local queue for validations and decisions
summary: Codex Checkpoint preserves pending validations, decisions and feedback across work sessions.
role: Product direction and development of the native application, from the interface to the mechanisms that preserve pending work across sessions.
evidence: Card imports with duplicate-safe keys were validated in the local flow; the application also provides backup and recovery.
promise: Pending work resumes at the right time with context and decisions intact.
showcaseSubtitle: Keeps decisions, validations and pending work from being lost between work sessions, preserving context for the next step.
imageAlt: Codex Checkpoint showing a fictional queue of pending validations, decisions and note history

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Not every test can be completed during the session.
tabs.body: Playtesting, visual review, devices, authentication and practical decisions may require another moment or environment. Without a queue, that context disappears.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: A checkpoint queue — not another chat.
tabs.body: Each checkpoint records enough context to return to the pending task and leave a decision or actionable feedback.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: A native, installable application.
tabs.body: Interface, command line and file integration form one product. Current versions are not code-signed yet, and that limit remains clearly stated.

name: NEXUS
kicker: A Windows hub for local projects
summary: NEXUS brings projects, paths and checks into one local hub that shows what is ready and what needs attention.
role: Product direction and development of the local hub, including registration, safe path discovery and validations.
evidence: Startup without a connection, interface-based registration and safe path discovery were validated in the local base.
promise: The right path appears before execution — without hunting through shortcuts.
showcaseSubtitle: Centralizes projects, paths and validations to show what is ready and what still needs attention.
imageAlt: Current NEXUS overview with two fictional projects, readiness states, update dates and an option to add a project.

tabs.label: Problem
tabs.title: Multiple projects outgrew a pile of shortcuts.
tabs.body: Each product has its own versions, tools and checks; the right path needs to appear before anything runs.

tabs.label: Solution
tabs.title: A local command desk replaces the pile of shortcuts.
tabs.body: Projects and paths are added from the interface; NEXUS only adopts a newer alternative when the match is safe and unambiguous.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: The local hub is in use.
tabs.body: Projects and checks open in their development context, without a required login and without mixing product environments.

name: Local First Checklist
summary: An open-source checklist keeps tasks in a local file and provides simple operations without relying on a remote service.
role: Definition of the example, command-line implementation, tests, documentation and publication of version 1.0.0.
evidence: The public repository and v1.0.0 release make the code, documentation and published version available for inspection.
promise: A compact example for organizing tasks on the computer and inspecting how each part works.
showcaseSubtitle: Turns local-first principles into practical criteria for software with greater autonomy, privacy and control.
imageAlt: Illustration of a local checklist with completed items and a JSON file

tabs.label: Scope
tabs.title: Small enough to understand end to end.
tabs.body: Tasks remain in a local JSON file, with simple operations available through the command line.

tabs.label: Quality
tabs.title: Simplicity still needs evidence.
tabs.body: Unit tests, Python compilation and a smoke test protect the main operations without adding infrastructure to the application.

tabs.label: Status
tabs.title: Version 1.0.0 is published.
tabs.body: The published version brings together structure, documentation, tests and a coherent architectural choice within a limited scope.

name: C7 Engineering System
kicker: The engineering method behind my products
summary: C7 supports the principles I follow when building products: clear context, rigor proportional to risk, and evidence before completion.
role: Method conception, system architecture and validation of the installed version.
evidence: Version 1.0.0 brings together core tests, installed-environment checks, comparative evaluations and restoration in a disposable profile.
promise: A consistent method for different problems, risks and deliveries.
showcaseSubtitle: Brings together the principles I use to decide, build, verify and evolve each product.
imageAlt: C7 Engineering System organizing complex flows around a core with seven balanced facets
cardImageAlt: Project flows converging on the C7 monogram and seven coordinated facets

tabs.label: Context
tabs.title: Context comes before execution.
tabs.body: Before building, I define the problem, audience, scope and completion criteria. This reduces rework and protects product coherence.

tabs.label: Risk
tabs.title: Rigor follows impact.
tabs.body: Simple tasks remain simple. As reach, cost of error or difficulty of reversal increases, I deepen analysis, validation and recovery.

tabs.label: Evidence
tabs.title: Completion requires evidence proportional to the change.
tabs.body: Version 1.0.0 passed the core Pester suite, installed-environment checks, comparative evaluations and a restoration test in a disposable profile.

tabs.label: Environment
tabs.title: The plan respects available capacity.
tabs.body: I organize stages and validation around CPU, memory, paging and storage, avoiding repetition of work already proven.

tabs.label: Continuity
tabs.title: Valid work should not need to be repeated.
tabs.body: I record decisions, tests and resumption points so each stage begins from the project’s actual state.
